subject: economics
title: PED and Revenue
welcome_lead: PED tells you whether a price change raises or cuts revenue.
meta_desc: A-Level PED: revenue test and price-setting.
final_note: Raise price on inelastic goods; cut price on elastic ones.

concepts.def: PED above 1: price cut raises revenue; PED below 1: price rise raises revenue.
Extra revenue from one more unit sold.
Inelastic - small PED, large share of essential consumption.
Firm with discretion over price (monopoly or differentiated good).

walkthroughs.body_html: If PED is inelastic, raising price boosts revenue - the quantity falls less than price rises. If PED is elastic, cutting price boosts revenue.
Cigarettes - inelastic - bear heavy tax because price rises raise revenue more than they cut volume. Cinema tickets - more elastic - get discounted on midweek to fill seats.
Firms with pricing power test PED through experiments and price A/B tests. Software firms vary prices by segment to exploit different PEDs - student vs business pricing.

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.

mcqs.q: What does Income Elasticity of Demand (YED) tell us?
options: Revenue is profit before tax and profit is revenue after tax.
The sign tells us the good type: positive YED = normal good (rises with income); negative YED = inferior good (falls with income). YED > 1 indicates a luxury; YED between 0 and 1 a necessity.
A negative YED means the demand calculation went wrong.
YED measures how the rich and poor differ in tastes.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between revenue and profit?
options: Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity); profit is what remains after deducting costs from revenue.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
Revenue and profit mean the same thing.
Revenue is profit before tax and profit is revenue after tax.
